- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop sharply, missing subsequent mean-reversion or downward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots and fails to adjust downward, leading to overcorrection or lagged correction.
- Model underestimates downward trends in later days of the 30d window, particularly when true values show persistent decline.
- Forecasts show strong persistence of recent highs, failing to account for volatility decay or seasonal/structural shifts.
- Model exhibits bias toward higher values when history includes recent high volatility or spikes.
- Correction should reduce forecast magnitude by 5–10% for early periods and adjust downward for periods with confirmed downward momentum.
- Avoid overfitting to recent high values; apply smoothing or decay factor to recent history when forecasting.
- When true outcome shows mean reversion, model should reduce forecast by 3–5% per day until convergence to historical mean.
